title: Credibility assessment of two CFD models for an intravascular catheter’s trackability and flow resistance within the ASME V&V 40 framework
device: Over-the-wire intravascular catheter intended for coronary and peripheral navigation and infusion

models.name: Model-Lumen-RANS (MLR)
models.what_it_computes: Steady incompressible RANS of the catheter’s internal lumen and side ports to predict pressure drop versus flow, wall shear stress, and entrance/exit loss coefficients under prescribed flow rates.

models.name: Model-Nav-NarrowGap (MNNG)
models.what_it_computes: Transient CFD in the pericatheter narrow gap using lubrication approximations within tortuous vessel geometries to estimate hydrodynamic drag during advancement, near-wall shear at contact, and pressure fields influencing trackability.

mechanisms.name: Tortuous-path bending and torsion during navigation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Resistance to advancement and steering through compound curvatures drives the push force required and the risk of buckling or loss of tip control (trackability).

mechanisms.name: Guidewire–catheter sliding friction within the distal lumen
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Friction along the wire–lumen interface modulates deliverability and can dominate incremental push force in tight anatomies (trackability).

mechanisms.name: Lumen viscous pressure drop under steady infusion
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Viscous losses set the flow resistance and affect achievable infusion rates and upstream pump pressures (flow resistance).

mechanisms.name: Entrance/exit losses and side-hole mixing under pulsatile delivery
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Unsteady local losses and port interactions add to mean pressure drop and influence jet patterns relevant to hemolysis and drug dispersion (flow resistance).

deviation.detail: All credibility factor scores are reported on a 0–12 numeric scale defined for this study (0 = no credible evidence; 12 = compelling, decision-grade evidence).

sections: 1. Background and objective

2. Context of Use (CoU): CFD predictions will be used to support design selection and design verification for catheter trackability and flow resistance across specified bench test conditions representative of indicated coronary and peripheral anatomies; results will inform test matrix reduction and acceptance rationales, not clinical decisions.

3. Model risk under ASME V&V 40: Medium model risk — influence is moderate (supports but does not replace bench verification), consequence of an incorrect prediction is moderate (potential suboptimal design leading to higher push force or pressure drop, mitigated by required bench testing); rationale: decisions bounded to preclinical verification with defined acceptance limits, with independent safety reviews.
4. Computational models: geometry definition, physics, boundary conditions, and solution strategies (MLR and MNNG)
5. Mechanisms assessed and mapping to quantities of interest
6. Credibility plan: factors evaluated, evidence sources, and scoring method (0–12 scale)

7. Model inputs (clear): specification of flow rates, waveform shapes, fluid properties, wire–lumen friction coefficients, curvature radii, and vessel path geometries for each mechanism; provenance and ranges
8. Numerical solver error (clear): mesh/time-step refinement procedures, residual controls, and observed solution changes per model and mechanism
9. Output comparison (clear): quantitative comparisons to flow-loop pressure–flow curves, pulsatile loss coefficients, and navigation push-force metrics from tortuous-phantom tests for each mechanism

10. Relevance of the quantities of interest (clear): mapping from computed fields (pressure drop, loss coefficients, hydrodynamic drag, near-wall shear) to acceptance metrics (trackability index, flow resistance thresholds) for each mechanism
11. Relevance of validation activities to the CoU (clear): justification that selected bench tests span the intended anatomy classes, wire sizes, and flow regimes tied to labeling
12. Test conditions (clear): matching of fluid analogs, temperature, catheter-wire assembly, curvature libraries, and flow loops to in-IFU ranges; instrumentation accuracy
13. Use error (passing mention): operator technique and setup nuances noted qualitatively alongside the validation protocols
14. Credibility scorecards (private 0–12 scale): per-model × per-mechanism factor scores
